name: Jupp Heynckes
scopeNote: Counted spells (proposed by the researcher on the caller's instruction, to be confirmed): Bayern Munich 2011-07-01 to 2013-06-30 (2012/13 treble; 2011/12 runner-up in all three competitions plus the lost 2012 CL final) and Bayern Munich 2017-10-06 to 2018-06-30 (return after Ancelotti; Bundesliga title, CL semi-final). These are the spells with real tactical coverage and titles; the catalog narrows a 1979-2018 career to its signature era. Spell dates come from memory plus the Bayern Strikes URL date (2017-10-06) and need a second source before use. Style terms used by sources: a 4-2-3-1 morphing to a 4-4-2(-0) block, 'position-orientated zonal marking' (Spielverlagerung) combined with situational man orientation in counter-pressing (Spielverlagerung 'access-oriented' counter-pressing), a mid-to-high compact block with two pressing zones in 2017/18, wide wingers plus fullbacks, direct counterattacking in Europe. A popular label 'gegenpressing side like Klopp' is not quite right: Bleacher Report says containment-based balance, Spielverlagerung measured fewer interceptions and more provoked challenges than Dortmund or Barcelona, and Heynckes said he wanted a balance between offence and defence. Several Wembley/2012-13 sources are retrospective (marked retrospectiveOnly) and BTL's 'man-mark vs zonal' sentence on the centre-backs contradicts Spielverlagerung's 'position-orientated zonal marking'. Partial dates (season) used where the match day was not in the source. The last spellsExcluded entry (earlier career) uses year-only dates because it groups several clubs.
openQuestions: Marking: Spielverlagerung (contemporary, 2013) says 'position-orientated zonal marking' in the 4-4-2-0 block, with Barca's wingers man-marking; Breaking The Lines (2022) says the centre-backs man-marked and did not zonally mark; Bayern Strikes (2018) says 'man-oriented pressing'. Treat Bayern as zonal block with situational man orientation when pressing/counter-pressing; confirm.

Real Madrid 1997/98 (Champions League winner) is excluded from counted spells only because no tactical coverage was found (searches returned results, lineups, and dismissal stories). Confirm the user is happy with this; Goal Espana reports Sanz said he lost the dressing room and gives 28 May 1998 as exit, another summary says 8 days after the final (20 May) and Sanz said two days later.
Spell dates need a second source: Bayern 1 July 2011 start and 30 June 2013 end; return 6 October 2017 and end 30 June 2018 (2017 date only from a Bayern Strikes URL).
Leverkusen 2009-11: The Hard Tackle says he took over 'in the summer of 2010', which is probably wrong (he started 2009); only 2010/11 4-4-2/4-2-3-1 variation sourced, so excluded.
The Lewandowski 'I'm the boss' episode date was not found in the reading.

Squad-building dimension is thin: youth promotion (Alaba, Kroos, 2011) and Kimmich/Coman 2017 are sourced; Rotation at Bayern 2012/13 is only partly evidenced (Kroos rotating) and 2017/18 sources show a settled Stammelf; Sport1 pieces on rotation were read only as search summaries.
UEFA pieces ('Bayern's Barcelona master plan', 'Klopp and Heynckes compared') and fcbayern.com interviews were not accessible; the 2013 semi-final plan from Heynckes himself is missing.
